newsitem.title: UK: UK cabinet meets Tuesday on spending, no deal seen.
newsitem.headline: UK cabinet meets Tuesday on spending, no deal seen.

text.p: The British cabinet meets on Tuesday in an initial effort to agree departmental spending totals for 1997-8, but government sources said there is little prospect of an agreement being reached at the meeting.

Some Conservative Members of Parliament are convinced the political fortunes of the government hang on how much the so-called control total for total spending can be squeezed below the 268.2 billion stg target in last year's budget.
"I expect we will be in a position tomorrow for the cabinet to have a first run around the course," an official in Prime Minister John Major's office said.
He said it would not be at all unusual for ministers to have a series of cabinet meetings before reaching an accord.

Officials declined comment on British press reports of a confrontation between Chief Secretary to the Treasury William Waldegrave and Health Secretary Stephen Dorrell over spending on the National Health Service.
The Guardian newspaper quoted one unnamed source as saying Dorrell was "going to the wire" in his demand for an increase of nearly one billion stg in real terms for the 34 billion stg a year service.
The government has to agree on spending for all departments in time for Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke to frame his November 26 budget statement.
The more spending can be restrained, the greater is likely to be Clarke's elbow room for voter-pleasing tax cuts ahead of a general election, which must be held by May 22.
But even if agreement were reached on Tuesday, the government would not announce its spending plans until Clarke makes his budget statement.
They are traditionally published in the Red Book which accompanies the budget, officials noted.
